signs.h2: Signs Your Chimney Needs A Sweep
signs.p: If one of these sounds familiar, it is time.
signs.h3: It’s Been A Year Or More
signs.p-2: Or you don’t know when it was last done. Most wood-burning chimneys benefit from a yearly sweep.
signs.p-3: Buildup narrows the flue, so smoke doesn’t draw up the way it should.
signs.p-4: Creosote deposits smell, especially in humid weather.
signs.p-5: Soot and creosote falling from above mean there is buildup in the flue.
signs.p-6: You don’t know how the last owner used it. A sweep and a look inside is the clean start.
signs.h3-6: Leaves Or Nests In The Flue
signs.p-7: Debris blocks the flue. It comes out during the sweep — and a cap keeps it out.
signs.p-8: Not sure which one you’re seeing? That is what the free inspection is for. Book it here or call {{site.phone}}.

faq.q: How often should a chimney be cleaned?
faq.p-2: Most wood-burning chimneys benefit from a yearly cleaning, but it depends on how much you burn, what you burn, and the chimney’s condition. After seeing yours, we’ll recommend an honest schedule — sometimes that means less often, not more.
faq.q-2: How much does chimney cleaning cost?
faq.p-3: This winter, a standard chimney sweep is {{site.offer_price}}, with the inspection included. Chimneys differ, so call {{site.phone}} and we will confirm the price for yours before booking.
faq.q-3: Will it make a mess in my home?
faq.p-4: Protecting your home is step one of every visit: floors and the fireplace area are covered before any tool comes out, and we vacuum as we sweep. The area is left the way we found it — or cleaner.
faq.q-4: How long does a cleaning take?
faq.p-5: It varies with the chimney’s condition and access. We’ll give you a realistic window when we confirm your booking, and we stay until it’s done properly.
faq.q-5: What if you find a problem during the cleaning?
faq.p-6: We show you — with photos — explain what it means in plain language, and give you a price if repair work makes sense. What happens next is always your call.
